{{Short description|French chemist (born 1931)}}
'''Yves Jeannin''' is a French chemist born on 11 April 1931 in [[Boulogne-Billancourt|Boulogne sur Seine]]. He is the son of Raymond Jeannin, [[architect]], and Suzanne Armynot du Chatelet. He married Suzanne Bellé in 1956 and has two children, Philippe and Sylvie, born in 1961 and 1969.

He is a corresponding member of the [[French Academy of Sciences|French Academy of sciences]]<ref name=":0">{{cite web|title=Académie des sciences|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Liste-des-membres-de-l-Academie-des-sciences-/-J/yves-jeannin.html|date=}}</ref> and Professor Emeritus at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]].

== Biography ==
Yves Jeannin studied at the [[École nationale supérieure de chimie de Paris|École Nationale Supérieure de Chimie de Paris]] (Engineer in 1954, graduation rank: first). His first job was at the IRSID for a sixteen-month stay in [[London]] at the [[Royal School of Mines]] with Prof. F.D. Richardson. He worked on the [[thermodynamics]] of the oxidation of [[iron]]-[[chromium]] [[alloy]]s. He is preparing a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] thesis in Physical Sciences (1962) under the supervision of Pr J. Bénard, on the crystallochemistry of [[titanium]] sulphides. In 1963, he spent a period in the United States as a Post-doctoral Research Associate of the [[United States Atomic Energy Commission]], [[Argonne National Laboratory]], and [[Iowa State University]].

He became a lecturer at the [[Paul Sabatier University]] of [[Toulouse]] in 1964, then Professor at the Pierre and Marie Curie University, Paris (UPMC), in 1974 where he taught in preparation for the medical school entrance examination at the [[Pitié-Salpêtrière Hospital|Pitié-Salpétrière Hospital]], in [[inorganic chemistry]], the Master of Chemistry at UPMC, the Master of Chemistry at L'[[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École Normale Supérieure]], the Advanced Study Diploma (DEA) in inorganic chemistry, the DEA in [[crystallography]], the preparation for the agrégation in chemistry at L'École Normale Supérieure.

Jeannin became head of the Chemistry group of the Lagarrigue Commission in charge of rebuilding the chemistry curricula of high schools (1976-1980). He was a member of the jury for the agrégation examination in chemistry (1971-1974), a member of the jury for admission to the École Normale Supérieure (9 years), and a member of the jury for admission to the [[École Polytechnique]] (2 years). At the request of the Ministry, he took part in the setting up of the internal agrégation in Physical Sciences (President of the jury, 1985-1988). He is a member of the Commission proposing to the Minister the General Inspectors, member of the recruitment jury of the Engineers of the [[Corps des mines|Corps of Mines]]. He will also be a chargé de mission at the French Ministry of Research (4 years).

Jeannin is a member of the University's Scientific Council, President of the Research Commission of the UFR of Chemistry, and a member of the Academic Council of the École Normale Supérieure.

== Scientific work ==
In research, Jeannin shows an interest in the chemistry of [[transition metal]]s, in the synthesis and structure of the species they form. First in solid state chemistry with the study of the [[Non-stoichiometric compound|non-stoichiometry]] of binary and ternary [[chalcogenide]]s of [[titanium]] and [[zirconium]],<ref>Y.Jeannin, J.Bénard, « Étude de la phase non-stoechiométrique TiS2 : étude du domaine et nature des défauts », ''C.R.Acad.Sc.'', 248, (1959), <abbr>p.</abbr> 2875</ref><ref>Y.Jeannin, A.Mosset, « Non-stoechiométrie du silicoséléniure de zirconium », ''J.Less Com.Met.'', 27, (1972), <abbr>p.</abbr> 237</ref> then he studies the [[iron]] complexes formed by [[solvation]] in non-aqueous media,<ref>G.Constant, J.C.Daran, Y.Jeannin, « Synthèse et propriétés d’une série de trichlorotricyanoferrates d’hydrogène non-stoechiométriques », ''C.R.Acad.Sc.'', 265, (1967), <abbr>p.</abbr> 808</ref><ref>G.Constant, J.C.Daran, Y.Jeannin, « Composé de coordination formé entre le chlorure ferreux et la formamide : catena μ-dichlorobis(formamido,O)fer(II) », ''J. Inorg, Nucl. Chem.'', 33, (1971), <abbr>p.</abbr> 4209</ref> the synthesis and [[X-ray crystallography|X-ray]] study of [[Organometallic chemistry|organometallic]] [[polymetallic]] species, and finally the chemistry of polyoxotungstates. In the latter case, it is essentially the compounds containing the XW9 brick that have attracted his attention.<ref>J.Martin-Frère, Y.Jeannin, « Synthesis and X-ray structure of the first mercury(I) containing polytungstate [(Hg2)2WO(H2O)(AsW9O33)2]10- », ''Inorg.Chem.'', 23, (1984), <abbr>p.</abbr> 3304</ref><ref>M.Alizadeh, S.Harlmaker, Y.Jeannin, J.Martin-Frère, M.Pope, « A heteropolyanion with fivefold molecular symmetry that contains a non labile encapsulated sodium ion. == Honours and distinctions ==

*   Member then Chairman of the Inorganic Chemistry Nomenclature Commission of the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry]] (IUPAC)
*   Member of the IUPAC Bureau, then President (1989-1991)
*   Correspondent of the French Academy of sciences (1980)<ref name=":0" /> (member of the Sealed Folds Commission, the Philosophy and History of Science Commission, the Metrology Commission, President of the French Committee of International Scientific Unions - COFUSI)
*   [[Doctor Honoris Causa]] of the [[University of Leeds]] (1990)
*   Winner of the [[Humboldt Prize|Alexander von Humboldt Prize]] (1990)
*   Visiting Professor at the Universities of [[Hamburg]], [[Heidelberg]] and [[Munich]] (Technische Universität)
*   Chevalier in the [[Ordre national du Mérite|Ordre National du Mérite]], Officier of the [[Ordre des Palmes Académiques]]
